_comment: kuksa-someip-provider's VehicleState client (SWARCH-001 §2). vsomeip parses JSON strictly and ignores unknown keys; "_comment" fields below are documentation only, never read by vsomeip.

services._comment: Remote VehicleStateService (SYS-002 §3.1, offered by vehicle-state-server). unicast/reliable here must match vehicle-state-server/config/vsomeip.json's own unicast and port exactly, since this is how the client locates it.

events._comment: EvVehicleState, SYS-002 §4.2. is_field is a static vsomeip hint; someip_client.cc's init_event_service() passes ET_FIELD explicitly on request_event(), which is authoritative here.

eventgroups._comment: EventGroupVehicleState, SYS-002 §4.2. is_multicast=false because SYS-002 §5.1 requires TCP-only delivery; no UDP/multicast event endpoint is configured.

service-discovery._comment: No explicit ttl here (unlike vehicle-state-server's): SWARCH-002 §7's TTL requirement is scoped to the offering side's OFFER entries (SYS-002 §5). This client only sends FIND/SUBSCRIBE entries, so it relies on the vsomeip stack default. cyclic_offer_delay is set explicitly because vsomeip also uses it (at 110%) as this client's own 'have I heard any multicast SD traffic lately' watchdog (service_discovery_impl::on_last_msg_received_timer_expired) -- the vsomeip default (~1000ms, i.e. a 1100ms watchdog) is shorter than autoas-as's native Sd stack's own OfferCyclicDelay (3000ms, Sd_ServerTimerDefault in autoas-as/src/infras/communication/SomeIp/SomeIp.c), so the watchdog fired continuously and vsomeip kept leaving/rejoining the multicast group without ever settling long enough to complete a subscription (autoas-as/src/app/fmw/README.md section 11.3). 4000ms gives margin above that 3000ms cadence.
